btos.label: Utilities (NAICS 22; oil and gas extraction reports under mining)

name: Energy
blurb: Grid optimisation, exploration, and the datacenter power crunch that makes energy both an AI user and AI's binding constraint, from EPRI and DOE to the utilities and oilfield majors.

points.desc: The Department of Energy's AI office covers grid, science, and security applications.
points.name: DOE runs the federal program

points.desc: DOE's datacenter electricity report - 4.4% of US power in 2023, 6.7 to 12% projected by 2028 - is tracked in this site's Power and Cooling section.
points.name: The power constraint is quantified

points.desc: The utility-backed Electric Power Research Institute runs the working groups on AI grid resilience, wildfire-risk prediction, and asset-health monitoring - the sector's shared research layer.
points.name: EPRI leads the utility research

points.desc: The Grid Modernization Initiative is the federal record of AI projects in real-time grid balancing, reactor optimization, and carbon capture across US utilities.
points.name: DOE funds the grid modernization

points.desc: The Power & Energy Society publishes the standards and research for machine learning in power systems, grid cyber-defense, and distributed energy resource management.
points.name: IEEE PES sets the technical standards

points.desc: The largest US renewable producer forecasts wind and solar yield, optimizes battery dispatch, and automates plant maintenance with AI - its own reporting is the deployment record.
points.name: NextEra applies AI to the renewable fleet

points.desc: The turbine and substation makers ship AI controllers and digital-twin software for gas, wind, and grid assets - where energy AI arrives as equipment.
points.name: Siemens Energy and GE Vernova build the digital twins

points.desc: Baker Hughes and Halliburton deploy AI for autonomous drilling, reservoir simulation, and pipeline monitoring; Shell and ExxonMobil run enterprise AI for seismic processing and predictive maintenance.
points.name: The oilfield services giants automate the subsurface

points.desc: Amperon's demand forecasting and Grid4C's smart-meter analytics are the specialist layer selling accuracy to utilities and energy desks.
points.name: Forecasting pure-plays serve the traders and utilities

points.desc: Computer vision on 3D seismic data, automatically mapping subsurface faults for oil, gas, and geothermal exploration.
points.name: Geoteric reads the seismic with deep learning

summary: Grid optimisation, exploration, and the datacenter power crunch make energy both an AI user and AI's binding constraint. Who tracks it: the utility research bodies and DOE are the primary record, with the grid and oilfield incumbents' own technology programs layered on top.
